summary: Jaladrishti addresses the urgent challenge of escalating groundwater depletion and unpredictable regional water scarcity across India by transforming multi-year terrestrial water storage data from NASA’s GRACE and GRACE-FO missions into accessible early-warning insights. By tracking long-term hydrological trends and subsurface aquifer changes from space, the project bridges the gap between raw Earth observation data and actionable decision-making, empowering local planners and communities to anticipate severe droughts and manage water resources proactively.
details: Jaladrishti ("Water Vision") is an Earth observation initiative that monitors groundwater depletion and forecasts regional water scarcity across India—including vulnerable areas like Hyderabad's Musi River basin—using satellite gravity data from NASA’s GRACE and GRACE-FO missions. By tracking multi-year terrestrial water storage anomalies and subtle gravitational shifts caused by changing underground aquifer levels, Jaladrishti identifies long-term drying trends and transforms complex NASA Earthdata into clear early-warning insights, empowering communities, farmers, and urban planners to anticipate severe water shortages and take proactive conservation action before crises hit.
